This... This is one of the biggest disappointments I've ever had with a video-game, period. They had the easiest home run in history, and I haven't seen such a big fumble in a LONG time.

I don't even know where to start. This game reeks of cynicism. And no, it's not the fact you only have one character unlocked... but it does start there: On Beta, you unlocked >TWO< for starters (Wonder Woman & Shaggy). In every other F2P game in existance there are plenty of fighter unlocks on your first few hours, maybe in a special set of missions and tracks, that set you up with a good, diverse cast of characters. Why didn't this game do that?

When you start the game, after the tutorial, you INSTANTLY get like.... what, 8 dailies? A thousand events and quests, no time to breathe, several notifications, and of course, a >LOADED. SHOP.<, that is miles and away the best UI & UX design across the entire game, squeaky clean and polished. Gee, I wonder why. In any other F2P game, there are slow introductions to each of those systems no matter what - There are fast level ups, and each level up unlocks a different system (Shop usually IS. NOT. ONE OF THE FIRSTS.) But no, we are forced into a tutorial (without even setting up controls as we'd like) and, as soon as it's done, there you go! Thousands of missions, hey shop is open! Oooh, can't do much of the PvE without characters and LOOT BOXES, can you? Guess you better start buying and/or grinding, chop chop! And here, have a thousand bots before you find a single person online!

The wording of the dailies is absurd, too - What's a "GUEST FIGHTER"? What are all these tags?! I get the beige teags like "Detective" and "Heroic" tags are meant for Neat lore introduction, good for PvE, good for finding general vibes... but it just... shouldn't really be a factor in PvP. It shouldn't appear period, like the Gems system doesn't. It confuses new players, and is unnecessary information overload. 

Oh yeah, I didn't talk about the gameplay yet: It's slow. Like, really, really, REALLY slow. I understand the reasoning, it's sound on paper - The beta was too fast and frenetic, and that doesn't appeal to the casual audience, the clear target audience here (And genuinely what you should aim for at least in majority when ideating a F2P game), and doubles, the combat design focus, was almost undecipherable without extreme knowledge. But they really, really, REALLY overcorrected here. Everything feels sluggish, NOTHING flows into NOTHING, ESPECIALLY NOT IN A CLEAR AND INTUITIVE WAY (Psst.... The Beta? Had advanced tutorials that told you about stuff like cancels. Not found here! :D ). The minutia of balancing doesn't matter all that much beyond the complete liquidation of manouverability , but there IS one thing they tried to solve: Without more advanced movement options, characters can't contest other far-away characters. Guess what they did... :D

They added a dash attack. But not only a regular dash attack, a dash attack that is not only CLEARLY incredibly busted for most characters, but also one that is UNAVOIDABLE if you're running. You can't walk and do your forrward attack anymore - something every single other platform fighter does, because they differentiate between "Walking" and "Running". No such differentiation in MultiVersus! Either input your forward attack within the first second of walking forwards, or you'll be dash attacking (Which is very vulnerable at high levels of play - the exact high levels of play you'd like to have the option of running and THEN doing your forward attack in a better position)

Parry was a nice addition, the game looks awesome... But there are still major connection issues in my anecdotal experience, there are still unpolished areas (Really? Same splash art when loading the game?) but there is no such thing as a perfect launch. If it were just one or two of all of these, I'd have been perfectly fine. But it isn't. And what's worse - If you're aiming for the casual crowd 90%, why didn't you release a NEW version? Steam doesn't like old games doing massive updates if they're not already something within their inner circle of connections and, without that knowledge, you guys are sitting ducks. MultiVersus isn't on the front page, it's not on "New and Trending", there's no banner for the grand launch. Please.... help me understand.

By the way, no native DualSense support despite the beta having it. :)

[b]There are a lot of things that let me down in the game and made me stop.[/b]

A week after the game was open for download for everyone I downloaded it and started playing with some friends, everyone was very hyped about the game, we played ALL day non-stop. The same day I started playing, I already bought the most expensive founder pack (which claimed to be there for a limited time) and continued at this pace of playing almost all day for a week or two, adding up to 120 hours of gameplay at the end. But what started to discourage me in the game was, first thing: repetitive maps and classes clearly too OP's. Some character combos are clearly broken, and it's something that I as a player understand is very difficult to balance (maybe impossible).

Smash games have this constant problem, developing a game like Multiversus is asking to work [b]FOR THE REST OF YOUR LIFE[/b], because with each new character to be released, ALL the others will be affected and their gameplay, skills, combos, timings will have to be readjusted, and that is at least hell for those who are developing.

So, the expected happens, the characters are completely broken, and the randomness of the character selection doesn't help this to work well, as we can fall against a team with two robots and I'm, I don't know, bugsbunny. Can you win? Maybe. Do I need skill for this? No, just luck. And this lucky is discouraging, because no matter how much you know how to play, you are at the mercy of losing to someone who doesn't even know how to play but uses a stronger character.

Not only that, but the INEXISTENCE of a ranked mode makes the game completely meaningless, as you click to play and you can fall against both a person who has just created the account, and someone who has already played 250 games on closed beta (happened to me), and obviously you can't have fun playing against someone extremely stronger than you, obviously. So one of the solutions for the game is to [b]CREATE THE RANKED[/b], it doesn't make sense that this doesn't exist until now!

Another thing that bothers me is the lack of variety, both in characters and maps. Obviously this is very difficult to build for a game like this, given what I mentioned above of having to "rebalance" the game with each addition, but at least the maps should have several. But how to make so many maps if we don't have ideas? [b]OPEN TO THE COMMUNITY! [/b]Do some kind of integration with the steam workshop, give prizes to winning maps, or something similar, just like CS:GO has its workshop tab for you to make skins, use this feature to add multiple maps (Speed​​Runners also do something similar). And this can also serve the characters themselves, ideas are what the community will not lack.

One more thing that bothered me deeply, and I say that not as a player but as a consumer, is the founding package not having the exclusivity it promised. In the early days of the game, a HUGE alert would appear on the screen that the founder packs would be exclusive and LIMITED time, giving the idea that at any moment it would leave the store. Marketing ploy? Maybe, but for the level of engagement that the game was, I wouldn't imagine that they would use a trick as dirty as this, mainly because it's [b]R$ 299,99[/b] (brazilian currency) and the only real exclusivity is a yellow name ːsteamfacepalmː. Well, in addition to the price absurdity and the little advantage of buying a package like this, I bought it with the idea of[b] ​​"encouraging development"[/b][spoiler](my worst mistake) [/spoiler] after all the package would be for a short time, as announced, and only those who helped in the beginning would have access to the exclusives that he provided. Congratulations, it just so happens that [b]the package is in store until today (29/09/22[/b] almost 2 full months after I bought the "limited time package" (31/07/22), and that didn't make me just angry because I was wronged as the package provides "3 battle passes" and the 15-category beta pass was counted as a pass, that's it, I paid for a REDUCED pass! For me, there's nothing I can do about all that I've said now, so I just feel wronged for having paid R$300 for something that SHOULD be exclusive.

Finally, I'm also unhappy with how difficult it is to get XP in the battle pass. If you have a merely healthy life and don't play 8 hours a day, you won't complete the pass. But I understand that this is the new way to "trapping players in the game", thank you Epic Games for that.

I really like the game, but even though I really enjoyed playing it [b] I decided to stop[/b] , because all this injustice and this feeling of "incomplete product" that the game brings, it's unfair to me that I paid all this amount to encourage this to have decent scope to be called a game.

They got rid of all the gold I accumulated and did not convert it to fighter currency - People that saved their gold instead of spending it to unlock every character got screwed out. I lost a ton of gold that could have unlocked all my characters. It's a poor decision by a company that claims they want to reward those that played their beta and stuck around for the shutdown/relaunch. Not a good move and the monetization seems to be worse than before, things like being unable to choose to use fighter points to unlock characters instead of the character tokens so you have to use them all up, skin prices misaligning with premium currency denominations so you have to spend $10 to get a "$5" skin because you're short a few gems, etc.

After following this game from the reveal trailer, I genuinely believe this game was a labor of love by its developers that deserved the time and attention of so many more players than it had at peak numbers. The potential this game realized, let alone what it never did realize, is a testament to the love the studio had for this concept, and I hope they all move to bigger and better things and that someday this format can be attempted again. Live service for a platform fighter remedies so many of this genre's problems and the biggest failure in the case of MultiVersus is WB's sudden realization that in general, live service is unnecessary. I think MultiVersus is a tragic case of collateral damage from WB's repeated and erratic under and over-commitments to live service after this realization, and that all it really needed was better structure. I could get into the nuance of this, and am willing to if anyone wants to discuss, but at this point this review is meant to be a eulogy to a game I truly loved, even when I hated it. Someday this game will be used to improve another game of the same type, and that alone is worth its existence and the resulting controversies.

[h3] PFG took all the player feedback from the Open Beta and seemly fixed everything that was criticized [/h3], there is a lot of offline content, mini games, a great season 1 battle pass (that you get enough currency to pay for the next season), local game with bots, the perk system was redesigned, a lot of visual polish on the characters and animations, 4 more characters next to the release and a lot of little teasers for coming ones.

[h3] But every change that they made on their own made the game worst and less fun: [/h3]

[olist]
     [*] The combat is slowed down to a halt.
No more skill expression through quick movement, dodge and jump cancels and situational combos. Now matches are decided on the basis of a very slow whiff punishing dance, which in one hand is good since combat is more deliberate and neutral focused, but it's just less fun overall. For me, the best thing about this game was the movement options it gave the player and that is simply gone. (The game is also unbalanced but it's expected on release)

   [*] No ranked matches?
It took a long time of open beta to for ranked to finally be added to the game, and it's missing on release, what's up with that?
 
  [*] No Lab
Now we have a training mode with less features, and you can no longer practice with characters you do not own

  [*] No Global and Character Rankings on the Career profile
you used to be able to see you raking on a global ranking system, witch was a pretty cool feature, a global high score was a game of itself.

  [*] Everything on the end of battle screen
You could see how much damage was done, how many ring-outs, etc. This was a cool feature that should have been enhanced, but it was took out entirely. You also can no longer see when people accept or decline the rematch, you don't have a social menu to add as friend, block or view the profile anymore nor have the option to toast back, [b] It's ALL gone [/b]

  [*] No Character Select during rematches
During rematches you were able to change character and cosmetics, you had some time to strategise your rematch, see which character would be best, what perks worked and not, and play around with emotes, Skins, badges and etc. It's all gone, if you happen to have a bad match up, all you can do is infinitely rematch, maybe change perks if you did a custom set beforehand

  [*] The Zoom
I'm not sure this is a bug or a design decision, but the zoom on the characters when they are close by is so much that it even cuts any of the emotes equipped. It's distracting and you can't see much of the map, on a game that has to many variables of destructible walls and other hazards, it just makes it difficult to plan anything.
[/olist]

There are many more things that I couldn't even be bothered to list, like the fact that PFG took out announcer packs that could only be obtained by buying them with real money, and the UI that is extremely confusing for no reason along with 4 different currency systems.

TL;DR:  It looks like a proper F2P full released game, but the game is not as fun anymore, sadly.

Multiversus could have been the perfect F2P fighting game. When it first launched, it was fast, felt great to play, and was full of charm - a great visual style, a fun and funny varied character roster and lots of potential. The developers clearly couldn't keep pace with the live service content machine - the same thing that kills so many live service games, and they decided to pretend the game had been in Beta and removed it from stores for a year to work on things. 

The problem is, when it came back it was actually worse in literally every way - the gameplay was slowed down and felt like you were underwater, they made the economy significantly worse and took away your resources and choices from the original launch, they took away a bunch of your rematch options and post-match stats to keep bad players from realizing how poorly they were doing, and despite taking away a game that people had paid $100 for a year to work on things, the content slowed down immediately afterwards again so the team could go back to trying to make fundamental mechanical changes again to reverse the damage they had done. 

It's no surprise they're pulling the plug on this game, but it is an absolute shame - they had the perfect template for something special, but WB and PFG made the wrong choices at literally every potential junction. Too slow to update, while shooting itself in the foot with every patch. This was one of my favorite experiences of the generation at its initial launch, but as it dies a quiet, unmarked death, I can only remember it as one of its biggest disappointments instead.

They really did a lot to make the game feel like a cheapened experience in their time away.

- failed to address issues with some of the stronger characters from the beta while severely nerfing some of the characters who were struggling
- You no longer earn battlepass xp for simply playing. This means once you finish challenges (which you can do in an hour) you are no longer working towards anything.

On average, most skins are $10. This doesn't even include the crazy grind to unlock characters, which could theoretically take 150+ hours. Even if you wanted to play the PvE mode (Rifts), you'd still have to grind out gems to unlock higher difficulties or pay for a set of randomized gems.
On top of this, the game has been plagued by netcode issues, missed hits, and being consistently matched against players a whole tier above your own in Ranked! While the developers do seem to respond to feedback, it's unfortunate that somewhere up the corporate ladder, they decided to neglect the game. At its core, the game is still a product of love and care. I still believe in the game and the developers behind it, which is why I continue to play. It seems that with Season 3, they attempted to fix a lot of the issues the community has mentioned, which gives me hope for the future of MVS. Unfortunately, the damage is done. Platformers in general have a small community, and making the price of entry so steep is a definitive way to isolate your game from the playerbase and rest of the great platformers out there where you won't have to spend 100 hours to start having fun. As much as I’d like to recommend this game, at this point in time, However I hope to do so in the future.

[h1]Overall[/h1]
At a surface-level, MultiVersus combines Super Smash Bros. mechanics with a more hack-and-slash style of combat. Casual players and thrill-seekers are sure to welcome the fast-paced action with open arms - if that's you, this is your game! However, more methodical, hardcore players are likely to become frustrated by the low cooldown and start-up frames of most attacks, the unclear hitbox sizes, and the lack of hitstun, leading to a watered-down strategical gameplay experience.

[h1]Pros:[/h1]
- Polished visuals
- Polished sound design
- Fun character gameplay designs - goofy moments galore
- Character balanced, while still flawed in many ways, is overall very decent for a newly released fighter.
- With the ability to customize your character taunts, out-of-bounds (death) animations, and loading screen flairs (think token system in LoL) via your account/character progress, you'll eventually have a wealth of customization options to choose from.
- Continuing from the above point, the payment model is clearly more cosmetics-focused, which I categorize as a good thing.

[h1]Cons:[/h1]
- For the time being, the time it takes to grind up gold to buy characters seems bit too slow, even for a free-to-play game. Gold-gain is much better paced toward buying perks.
- Attack animations do not currently cleanly match their hitboxes. This makes for some very confusing character attack interactions.
- The attack descriptions in the game, while good to have, do not provide enough information for more hardcore players to derive much meaningful info from them. (attack startup frames/cooldowns, hitboxes, hitbox frames, etc.)
- See the section at the bottom of this review for thoughts from a long-time SSB competitor regarding strategy.

[h1]Mixed:[/h1]
- The "cave of life" in the Scooby's Haunted Mansion stage can lead to frustrating or funny moments, depending on your disposition toward stage hazards.
- Currently there is no ranked mode, though there are matchmaking-rating leaderboards for the casual gameplay 1v1 and 2v2 modes. As indicated in the menu options, the devs clearly plan to launch a ranked mode at some point.
- The perks system, while interesting in terms of the customization options available to augment any given strategy, adds a bit of a pay-to-win element to the game. Reason is - the perks cost gold to train, which is the same currency used to buy characters. If your goal is strictly to win, you need to have a variety of perks to match any given team, opponent, or stage set-up. However, if you want quicker access to characters to learn their ins and outs in PvP, you will be at a stat (perks) deficit compared to your opponents - Think runes in the early days of LoL.

[b]It's worth noting that the characters in the game cost different amounts of gold. If you buy the character tokens/collector's pack with real money, I highly recommend not using them on the cheaper characters. Instead, to be more efficient with your time/money, dedicate your gold toward the more expensive characters.[/b]

---

[h1]Personal Notes:[/h1]
I compiled a list of cons that affect me specifically from a strategical point of view, as a former SSB professional/semi-pro. Please note that the game is still in Beta and it's very possible that some or all of these will eventually be addressed by the game team. These are just my opinions.

[b]Slow pace of neutral[/b]
Neutral = game state in which no characters have been hit, and none are off-stage

Button mashing, while still bad play from a strategical standpoint, unfortunately cannot be punished on reaction quite as frequently as one would expect. Aerials, airdodging, grounded attacks - The animations are so quick from start to end, that players are encouraged to use attacks even with the understanding that their attacks are likely to miss.

This has the potential to dramatically slow down the pace of neutral if you plan on playing in a calm, collected, methodical manner - think SSBB Mr. Game & Watch upsmash and SSBB Metaknight forward-smash levels of cooldown frames on many, many attacks, both grounded and aerial.

While character movement speed is indeed very fast, the pace of combat, before landing hits, can be quite tedious and slow as a result of the above. This leads to a very boring neutral unless you play mages (projectile users in MultiVersus).

[b]Avoidance[/b]
The character movement speed, while overall fast, fluid, and fun in its own right - when combined with the amount of movement, dodging, and directional airdodging options available - makes for a frustrating time chasing down opponents that choose not to interact. This makes it feel like being above an opponent or offstage is not as much of a disadvantage as it maybe should be.

[b]Low combo potential[/b]
The movement options in the game are quick, but hitstun is very, very low and dodging options are plentiful (think Super Smash Bros Brawl levels of hitstun and dodging options, but on steroids). This shifts your focus while in advantaged states (after hitting someone) away from comboing as the advantaged player, and interacting as the disadvantaged player via knockback influence, more toward a rock-paper-scissors-style of guessing game about which option your opponent is going to choose to get out of what could be a nice, short combo.

As others have already mentioned, Multiversus™ is a platform fighter that takes a lot of influence from Nintendo®'s Super Smash Bros™ series of games.  I have always been an avid fan of the Super Smash Bros™ series; from the original Nintendo 64 release in 1999, to the most recent Super Smash Bros­­™: Ultimate game, released in 2018.  There have been a few other platform fighters that have tried to mimic the feel of Super Smash Bros™, many of them ending up falling short for one reason or another, but Multiversus™ has gotten very close to to bring back this awesome feeling.  I think that Multiversus™ is the best Super Smash Bros™ alternative out there.

A unique characteristic about Multiversus™ is that it strongly pushes a cooperative gameplay mechanic.  This is something that not even Super Smash Bros™ has implemented, as Team Matches over there disable any interaction among teammates.  But with Multiversus™, you're able to do such things as boosting your teammate by acting as a platform or roping them back to safety when they've run out of jumps in an otherwise bad situation.  I think this is an excellent way to mix up the formula a bit, and would get even better when playing locally around friends.

My main criticism about Multiversus™ would be its use of a Battle Pass, level-based XP system, and in-game Store¹.  This is kind of a minor criticism, as many other games seem have been doing these things for awhile now.  It does seem to be possible to unlock everything through simply playing the game, albeit slowly.  Although it can feel a bit overwhelming, or tedious at times, the fact that each character has its own level-based unlocks does motivate people to try new characters and play styles.  Often times with fighters, I have noticed that people tend to stick with one, or a few, "main characters;" and this could potentially be a good move from Multiversus™ to try and persuade players away from this tendency.

Amazing fresh take on the Platform Fighter Genre. Insane amounts of content just for playing, and in general an amazing experience all the way through. Every aspect of the game is meant for the intended doubles format. It isn't just slapped on haphazardly. From the perk synergy to the movement, everything about this games actual mechanics is both unique enough to stand out, but familiar enough to get into.

The character interactions are amazing as well, something that I didn't know I needed in a platform fighter until now. There are unique voice lines for specific match ups on start up, as well as unique defeat/victory quotes, and mid match quotes that really liven up the experience. The game is chock full of love for each characters respective legacy.

The only down side I can see becoming a problem in the future is the monetization. I purchased the founders pack which gave me basically all of the characters right away, as well as the battle pass, but I can see others getting impatient and buying the in game currency to get new wring outs, banners, etc. etc. 

Overall, this game has a bright future ahead of it. Fingers crossed.
